papers.title: A hierarchical deep reinforcement learning-model predictive control framework for lithium-ion battery fast charging under expansion-force constraints
papers.abstract: Fast charging of lithium-ion batteries is constrained by the trade-off between charging efficiency and physical safety, especially when high-current operation narrows the admissible electrical, thermal, and mechanical margins. Traditional model-based controllers can explicitly handle constraints, but their performance depends on model fidelity and may become conservative near safety boundaries. In contrast, model-free deep reinforcement learning (DRL) provides flexible sequential decision-making but does not by itself guarantee hard safety-constraint satisfaction. This study presents a multi-stage constant-current (MCC)-inspired hierarchical DRL–model predictive control (MPC) framework that couples staged-current policy search with MPC-based safety correction under expansion-force constraints. Expansion force is incorporated as a dynamic safety constraint together with terminal voltage and surface temperature, allowing their coupled responses to be considered during control. A long short-term memory (LSTM)-based surrogate model is developed to predict battery-state evolution and support control-oriented optimization. Independent trajectory- and C-rate-holdout tests are used to examine its multi-step prediction error. Based on the surrogate predictions, the upper DRL layer selects candidate staged-current actions, whereas the lower MPC layer performs quadratic-programming (QP)-based safety correction before execution. Comparative simulation results against 3C constant-current (CC), native MPC, and pure DRL baselines show that the proposed method reaches 90% state of charge (SOC) in 728 s and improves the comprehensive score by 23.02%, 6.53%, and 11.64%, respectively. The reported trajectories remain below the prescribed voltage and temperature limits and the MPC expansion-force operating envelope.

papers.title: Physics informed neural network framework for non-similar nano-heat and solutal transport in a rheological fluid over a stretching cylinder
papers.abstract: Accurate prediction of non-similar momentum, thermal and solutal transport phenomena in rheological fluids is crucial for the design and optimization of advanced thermal management systems, heat exchangers, polymer processing, chemical reactors, energy conversion devices and biomedical transport processes. Motivated by these engineering applications, this study presents a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework for analyzing magnetohydrodynamic mixed convection flow of a Jeffrey fluid over a stretching horizontal cylinder embedded in a Darcy porous medium. The mathematical model incorporates the coupled effects of magnetic field, porous resistance, thermal radiation, Brownian diffusion, thermophoresis, viscous dissipation, velocity slip, internal heat generation, and Arrhenius activation energy along with chemical reaction. Owing to the non-similar nature of the governing equations, the Local Non-Similarity method is employed to transform the governing partial differential equations into a coupled system of ordinary differential equations, which is subsequently solved using a PINN implemented in PyTorch. The suggested algorithm is evaluated and tested with the help of BVP4C solver and shows good consistency with low $$\:{L}^{2}$$ error value of $$\:3.5\times\:{10}^{-3}$$ and stable convergence throughout the training phase. The results reveal that the rise in value of magnetic parameter reduce the velocity of fluid due to the Lorentz force while increase in Darcy number improves the flow due to decrease in porous effect. The thermal radiation and heat source have a major role to play in rising the temperature profile, while the increase in Schmidt number diminish the concentration distribution. The proposed LNS-PINN framework provides a computationally efficient procedure for simulating non-similar transport problems and offers a promising computational tool for engineering design and optimization of advanced systems.

papers.title: Global dynamics of dengue transmission with cryptic habitats and imperfect vaccination
papers.abstract: Motivated by the ongoing public health burden of dengue fever, this study presents a nine-dimensional dengue transmission model that incorporates imperfect vaccination and a phenomenological background effect associated with cryptic habitats. We derive the control reproduction number ( R c ) and examine the global stability of the disease-free and endemic equilibria. papers.title: Nano-chitosan-mediated salinity tolerance in Calendula officinalis: Nonlinear physiological thresholds and antioxidant responses identified via interpretable hybrid modeling
papers.abstract: Soil salinity severely constrains growth and phytochemical quality in medicinal plants. Chitosan-based biostimulants offer a promising strategy for stress mitigation, yet comparative assessments of conventional versus nano-chitosan under salinity, particularly when coupled with interpretable modeling, remain scarce. This study investigated the effects of four salinity levels (0, 50, 100, and 150 mM NaCl) and foliar applications of chitosan and nano-chitosan (0, 0.25, and 0.5 g L⁻¹) on morphological, physiological, and biochemical traits of Calendula officinalis under controlled greenhouse conditions. A hybrid interpretable modeling framework (IGANN–GPR) was developed that integrates generalized additive neural networks with Gaussian process regression, enabling both high-accuracy prediction and principled uncertainty quantification across fifteen plant response variables. The model achieved excellent performance (R = 0.84–0.99), with exceptional accuracy for photosynthetic pigments (R ≥ 0.98) and robust estimation of oxidative stress markers and secondary metabolites. Residual analysis confirmed unbiased predictions and stable generalization. Feature importance analysis revealed that nano-chitosan (35.9%) slightly outperformed salinity (34.0%) and conventional chitosan (30.1%) in influencing plant responses. Interpretable dose–response functions identified a distinct salinity threshold (~75 mM NaCl), beyond which growth and chlorophyll content declined sharply, while proline and phenolic compounds accumulated progressively. Nano-chitosan exhibited rapid sigmoidal activation at lower concentrations, suggesting enhanced bioavailability and more effective modulation of antioxidant enzymes and membrane integrity compared with conventional chitosan. These findings demonstrate that nano-chitosan alleviates salinity-induced oxidative damage by strengthening redox homeostasis and osmotic adjustment. By integrating predictive accuracy with mechanistic interpretability and uncertainty quantification, the proposed hybrid modeling framework offers a robust, transparent, and systems-level tool for understanding stress physiology and supporting precision management of medicinal crops under saline conditions.

papers.abstract: For young patients with osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), early adoption of appropriate hip-preserving surgery may prevent or delay the need for total hip arthroplasty (THA). To reduce soft-tissue and osseous disruption as well as simplify the procedure while maintaining clinical efficacy, we modified the “light bulb” procedure. This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy of the modified “light bulb” procedure for treating early-stage ONFH, and to analyze non-disease-related factors influencing femoral head survival, thereby establishing indications for this surgical technique. This retrospective study included 63 patients (70 hips) with early-stage ONFH who underwent the modified “light bulb” procedure at the Department of Orthopedics, Shanghai Sixth People’s Hospital, between September 2021 and June 2024. The cohort comprised 47 males (51 hips) and 16 females (19 hips), with ages ranging from 19 to 49 years. Patients were followed clinically and radiographically preoperatively, at 3 months, 6 months, 1 year postoperatively, and annually thereafter, with a minimum follow-up duration of 2 years. Clinical outcomes were evaluated based on serial assessments of patient demographics, Visual Analog Scale (VAS), and Harris Hip Scores (HHS) obtained preoperatively and at successive postoperative intervals. Radiographic follow-up included serial pelvic X-rays and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) obtained preoperatively and postoperatively to assess ARCO stage, China-Japan Friendship Hospital (CJFH) classification, collapse of femoral head, necrotic lesion area of femoral head and involvement area of articular surface. Hip preservation failure was defined as a composite endpoint, including HHS-defined functional failure, radiographic failure, or conversion to THA. HHS-defined functional failure was defined as a postoperative HHS below 80 points. Radiographic failure was defined as progressive femoral head collapse or the onset/progression of secondary osteoarthritis. Univariate logistic regression analysis was performed on the follow-up data to identify risk factors associated with clinical outcomes and radiographic progression, and Kaplan–Meier analysis was used to estimate femoral head survival rates. At the final follow-up (mean duration 23.9 ± 9.8 months), the overall hip preservation success rate was 71.4% (50/70 hips). Univariate logistic regression analysis revealed that CJFH L3 classification (OR 22.50, 95% CI 2.11–240.40, P = .010), ARCO IIIA (OR 7.43, 95% CI 2.35–23.48, P < .001), femoral head collapse (OR 7.43, 95% CI 2.35–23.48, P < .001), necrotic area > 30% (OR 7.11, 95% CI 2.06–24.54, P = .002), 15–30% articular surface area involved (OR 9.51, 95% CI 2.44–37.04, P = .001), corticosteroid use (OR 6.14, 95% CI 1.54–24.46, P = .010), high body mass index (BMI, OR 1.96, 95% CI 1.35–2.86, P < .001), and smoking (OR 5.29, 95% CI 1.73–16.12, P = .003) were significantly associated with the failed hip preservation. Kaplan–Meier analysis demonstrated that ARCO stage, CJFH classification, involvement area of articular surface, BMI, necrotic lesion area of femoral head, etiology, and smoking status significantly affected postoperative femoral head survival time. Therefore, involvement of the lateral pillar, ARCO stage IIIA, necrotic area > 30%, higher BMI, smoking, and steroid- or alcohol-induced osteonecrosis are all associated with poorer prognoses. At a mean follow-up of approximately 24 months, the modified “light bulb” procedure was associated with favorable hip-preservation outcomes in patients with early-stage ONFH, particularly in younger patients with lower BMI, earlier ARCO stage, and no lateral pillar involvement. By allowing debridement, decompression, and bone grafting of the necrotic region through a single tunnel, this technique may provide a tissue-sparing option for preserving the native hip. Longer-term follow-up is required to establish the durability of these outcomes and to further define the indications for this procedure.

papers.title: Neural augmented Lagrangian method for approximating viscosity solution of the eikonal equation
papers.abstract: Finding the viscosity solution of the eikonal equation with physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) is challenging, as methods that rely solely on the classical eikonal loss can converge to non-viscosity solutions rather than the viscosity solution. We propose a novel mesh-free PINN framework specifically designed to overcome this limitation. Our approach, which uses an implicit neural representation (INR) to model the solution, recasts the problem as a constrained optimization task rooted in the fundamental properties of the eikonal equation. To ensure convergence to the viscosity solution, our framework augments the standard PINN loss with a term derived from the equation’s variational form: maximizing the solution’s volume subject to a 1-Lipschitz gradient constraint. To robustly handle complex geometries with non-convex boundaries or holes, we further incorporate the Soner boundary constraint as an additional constraint. This constrained optimization problem is then transformed into an unconstrained objective using an augmented Lagrangian method (ALM), which provides rigorous and stable enforcement of all constraints during training. We demonstrate through experiments on a variety of challenging problems that our method successfully avoids spurious local minima and consistently converges to the viscosity solution, achieving relative L 2 errors on the order of 10 − 2 or less. Another advantage of the trained model is its ability to instantly recover the shortest time path from any point to the source, highlighting its practical value for applications in navigation and path planning.

papers.title: Synthetic diagnostics and integrated modeling: Bridging the gap between measurement and interpretation in magnetic confinement fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract In magnetic confinement fusion, we rarely measure physical quantities directly; instead, we measure their indirect signatures - photons, currents, and phase shifts. Bridging the gap between these raw signals and the physical parameters of interest (such as density or temperature) has traditionally relied on the inverse problem, a mathematical reconstruction process often plagued by ambiguity and ill-posedness. This tutorial advocates for a paradigm shift toward forward modeling via Synthetic Diagnostics. By processing simulation data through the same transfer functions as experimental instruments, we can translate theoretical predictions into synthetic signals, enabling a rigorous comparison with experiment. We formalize this approach within the TWINTOK framework, a Digital Twin architecture designed for systematic validation. Through detailed case studies - ranging from the spectroscopic evaluation of divertor detachment to the full-wave modeling of turbulence staircases - we demonstrate how synthetic diagnostics reveal physics that standard inversions often miss, such as the significant contribution of wall reflections to bolometric signals. As the community moves toward ITER and fusion power plants, where diagnostic access will be limited and interpretation challenging, this forward modeling approach provides the essential link to validate our predictive capabilities.

papers.title: Beyond Pricing Accuracy: A Multicriteria Diagnostic Benchmark of Neural Approaches to Financial PDE Approximation
papers.abstract: Neural approximations of financial PDEs are often ranked by aggregate pricing error, although price accuracy alone does not establish differential, physical, or financial consistency. We present a multicriteria diagnostic benchmark of seven representative configurations in a common Black–Scholes setting. The primary comparison uses a frozen 20,000-point test set and five optimization seeds; targeted three-seed controls examine domain truncation, collocation density, DGM update allocation and loss scaling, checkpoint selection, Hybrid order and activation, and Monte Carlo path allocation. Evaluation covers price and Greek errors, PDE residuals and tails, financial-violation frequencies and magnitudes, regime performance, runtime, and seed variability. The MLP achieves the lowest primary price MAE, 0.0675 ± 0.0057, whereas the Standard PINN at Smax = 400 achieves the lowest primary PDE MAE, 0.2648 ± 0.0432. The data-first Hybrid is competitive on both and obtains the lowest Greek errors and NEG, LBV, and monotonicity-violation frequencies. Moving Smax from 200 to 400 reduces PINN price MAE from 2.596 to 0.212, whereas extension to 800 raises it to 0.402; restoring collocation density does not recover Smax = 400 performance. Increasing DGM allocation from one to 20 updates per epoch reduces its PDE MAE from 0.4539 to 0.1498, below the matched-seed PINN value of 0.2662, but raises training time from 230.6 to 3022.4 seconds. Hybrid and checkpoint controls reveal criterion-specific trade-offs, while path-count diagnostics quantify stochastic-target noise. No configuration is uniformly dominant. Reliable neural-PDE benchmarking requires joint reporting of accuracy, physical and financial consistency, protocol choices, and cost.

papers.title: Low temperature mechanical behavior of additively manufactured stainless steels
papers.abstract: Η ευρεία χρήση κρυογονικών τεχνολογιών σε τομείς όπως η αεροδιαστημική βιομηχανία και τα κρυογονικά συστήματα αποθήκευσης καυσίμων καθιστά σημαντική τη μελέτη και την κατανόηση της μηχανικής συμπεριφοράς των δομικών υλικών σε χαμηλές θερμοκρασίες. Υπό αυτές τις συνθήκες, η μηχανική συμπεριφορά των μετάλλων μεταβάλλεται σημαντικά, επηρεάζοντας την αντοχή και την ολκιμότητα. Έτσι, για την κάλυψη των απαιτήσεων που προκύπτουν, θεωρείται αναγκαία η επιλογή υλικών που μπορούν να διατηρούν υπό αυτές τις συνθήκες. Παράλληλα, η ανάπτυξη των τεχνολογιών Additive Manufacturing έχει ενισχύσει το ερευνητικό ενδιαφέρον για τη μελέτη της επίδρασης της μικροδομής στη μηχανική συμπεριφορά των μετάλλων καθώς οι ιδιαίτερες συνθήκες κατασκευής μπορούν να επηρεάσουν σημαντικά τη μικροδομή και κατ’ επέκταση τις μηχανικές τους ιδιότητες. Οι ωστενιτικοί ανοξείδωτοι χάλυβες παρουσιάζουν ιδιαίτερο ενδιαφέρον, καθώς χρησιμοποιούνται ευρέως σε εφαρμογές χαμηλής θερμοκρασίας λόγω της ευνοϊκής τους αντοχής σε ψαθυρή θραύση. Συγκεκριμένα, οι 304L και 316L βρίσκονται μεταξύ των πλέον διαδεδομένων υλικών που αξιοποιούνται για κρυογενικές εφαρμογές καθώς χαρακτηρίζονται από υψηλή αντοχή και ολκιμότητα ακόμη και σε χαμηλές θερμοκρασίες. Επιπλέον, η συμπεριφορά των συγκεκριμένων κραμάτων σε κρυογενικές συνθήκες συνδέεται με πολύπλοκους μηχανισμούς παραμόρφωσης που επηρεάζουν τη μηχανική τους απόκριση. Η αυξανόμενη αξιοποίηση τους, σε συνδυασμό με την ανάπτυξη των τεχνολογιών Additive Manufacturing, οι οποίες οδηγούν στη δημιουργία μικροδομών που διαφοροποιούνται από εκείνες των συμβατικά παραγόμενων υλικών επηρεάζοντας τις μηχανικές τους ιδιότητες, αναδεικνύει την ανάγκη περαιτέρω διερεύνησης της συμπεριφοράς τους υπό κρυογενικές συνθήκες. Με βάση τα παραπάνω, η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία επικεντρώνεται στη διερεύνηση της θλιπτικής συμπεριφοράς των ωστενιτικών ανοξείδωτων χαλύβων 304L και 316L που έχουν κατασκευαστεί με τη μέθοδο Additive Manufacturing. Αρχικά, πραγματοποιείται βιβλιογραφική ανασκόπηση σχετικά με τις βασικές αρχές της τεχνολογίας Laser Powder Bed Fusion (L-PBF), τα μικροδομικά χαρακτηριστικά που αναπτύσσονται κατά τη διαδικασία κατασκευής, καθώς και τους μηχανισμούς παραμόρφωσης που ενεργοποιούνται στους ωστενιτικούς ανοξείδωτους χάλυβες υπό κρυογενικές συνθήκες. Στο πλαίσιο αυτό, ιδιαίτερη έμφαση δίνεται στη συσχέτιση της μικροδομής και της κρυσταλλογραφικής υφής με την ενεργοποίηση του φαινομένου Transformation Induced Plasticity (TRIP) και την επίδρασή του στη μηχανική συμπεριφορά των υλικών σε χαμηλές θερμοκρασίες. Παρουσιάζεται ο μηχανολογικός σχεδιασμός και η ανάπτυξη της πειραματικής διάταξης που προορίζεται για την πραγματοποίηση δοκιμών θλίψης σε διάφορες θερμοκρασίες. Για την επίτευξη και διατήρηση των επιθυμητών θερμοκρασιών δοκιμής, προβλέπεται διάταξη ελεγχόμενης ψύξης, στην οποία θα χρησιμοποιηθεί έγχυση υγρού αζώτου ώστε να εξασφαλίζεται η σταδιακή και ομοιόμορφη ψύξη των δοκιμίων κατά τη διάρκεια των δοκιμών. Η μελλοντική μελέτη θα περιλαμβάνει μηχανικές δοκιμές σε θερμοκρασία περιβάλλοντος καθώς και σε θερμοκρασίες 0°C, -50°C και -100°C, με στόχο την αξιολόγηση της επίδρασης της θερμοκρασίας στις μηχανικές ιδιότητες των υλικών.

papers.title: Electronic structure and multiscale modelling of the hydroxyapatite-TiO
papers.abstract: Hydroxyapatite-titanium dioxide (HA-TiO2) heterojunction coatings are commonly applied to enhance the osseointegration of load-bearing orthopedic implants, but their clinical performance is limited due to coating delamination and fibrous tissue encapsulation at the implant-bone interface. Density functional theory (DFT) offers excellent pre-synthesis predictions on HA-TiO2-based designs, but self-interaction error (SIE) remains a major hurdle due to the well-known underestimation of the band gaps of TiO2 and oxygen vacancy formation kinetics. This leads to inaccurate predictions of localized oxidative stress, electron transport, and early-stage corrosion at the interface. A comprehensive review of the accuracy-cost trade-off of DFT+U, hybrid functionals (HSE06), and machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for modelling the HA-TiO2 interface is given here. The electronic-structure corrections related to mesoscale phenomena accessible by molecular dynamics (MD) are also described. A systematic description of the stiff, ice-like hydration layer formed at the TiO2 surfaces is provided to shed light on the transport of Ca2+ and PO4 3- during biomineralization. Further, the dynamics of the hydroxyl dipoles, doping and nanostructuring that affect the nature and strength of the resulting interfacial adhesion energy are elaborated in detail. This multiscale approach that connects the accuracy of the electronic structure with the mesoscale hydration and ion-transport kinetics offers a physics-based, computationally informed path to the rational design of HA-TiO2 biomaterial coatings.

papers.title: Splat2Act: From Captured Scenes to Personalized VLA Manipulation
papers.abstract: A user who brings a generalist manipulation policy into their home or office wants it to pick up their objects from their shelves, counters, and tables. Yet even a strong generalist like $π_{0.5}$ achieves 0% pickup success in our captured deployment scenes without adaptation, and collecting real demonstrations in every user's environment is prohibitively expensive. We present Splat2Act, an automated real-to-sim-to-real pipeline that personalizes a pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) policy to a specific scene and object set using only a handheld phone scan and images of the user's objects. Unlike prior real-to-sim work that reconstructs individual tabletops, Splat2Act operates on building-scale indoor environments: it builds a photorealistic digital twin with 3D Gaussian Splatting and collision geometry, automatically discovers tabletop and non-tabletop receptacles, constructs feasible pickup tasks, and generates successful demonstrations with a privileged simulation oracle, with only scene and object capture required from a human. Applied to 101 scanned campus environments with a median navigable area of 104.87 m$^2$ and 7 receptacles, the pipeline yields 852 receptacles and over 68,000 pickup demonstrations. We fine-tune $π_{0.5}$ in two stages: Stage 1 adapts to hundreds of public object assets, drawn either from the deployment scene alone or from all 101 scenes; Stage 2 personalizes to the user's own objects on the deployment scene's receptacles. Our strongest personalized policy reaches 62.5% aggregate pickup success in the target scene. Deployed on a real Stretch 3, the same policy achieves 63.9% success on a 12-task subset, closely tracking its 66.7% simulated success on those tasks. These results suggest that automated real-to-sim-to-real training can personalize VLA manipulation policies using only simulation-oracle data.

papers.title: SLICE: Sequential Likelihood-Free Inference via Conformal E-Values
papers.abstract: Many scientific models can be simulated but have intractable likelihoods, making frequentist uncertainty quantification difficult. We construct exact anytime-valid confidence sequences for the parameters of such models. At each observation, fresh simulations from each candidate null conformalize a positive predictable score into a conditional e-value; their product is a test martingale, which we invert over the parameter. Validity holds for any such score, whatever its accuracy. We show that the oracle likelihood-ratio score maximizes expected log growth, which motivates approximating it with an amortized neural ratio estimator. On synthetic benchmarks, an audit of model routing in an LLM API, and microlensing data, the resulting confidence sequences stay valid under continuous monitoring, where fixed-sample methods do not, and neural scores remain competitive with exact likelihood ratios and application-specific scores.

papers.title: Dream to Remember: Continual Steering of Generalist Robot Policies with World Models
papers.abstract: Generalist robot policies are trained with imitation learning and are bounded by the quality and coverage of their demonstrations. Reinforcement learning can improve and extend them, either by fine-tuning the policy weights or by training a small module to steer the input noise of a frozen generative policy. When tasks arrive sequentially, both approaches suffer from catastrophic forgetting. Fine-tuning on a task degrades prior tasks, and steering only shifts forgetting to the shared steering module. We propose Dream to Remember (D2R), which continually steers a frozen generalist policy toward new tasks, while retaining its earlier skills. As the steering module learns a new task, a frozen pretrained world model rehearses prior tasks through imagined rollouts, anchoring the module to its earlier behavior without a replay buffer or new data. When the world model is faithful enough, D2R learns the new task entirely in imagination. Otherwise, it learns the task in the environment while using the world model only to rehearse prior tasks. On CALVIN, D2R improves eight tasks in sequence entirely in imagination, raising average success from 63.7% to 74.8%, while LoRA fine-tuning on the same sequence drops it to 11.7%. With a frozen off-the-shelf generalist policy and world model, $π_0$ and A2World, D2R learns unseen LIBERO-90 tasks in the environment while keeping $π_0$'s performance on the LIBERO suites it was fine-tuned on, even though the world model is not accurate enough for policy optimization. Finally, on a real Franka robot, D2R improves three tasks in sequence entirely in imagination while retaining the earlier improvements.

papers.title: Constrained Probabilistic Numerics: Gaussian Process Solvers for Linear PDEs under Linear Inequality Constraints
papers.abstract: Gaussian process solvers for linear partial differential equations (PDEs) return posteriors rather than point estimates, but they condition only on equality information: the PDE residual, boundary data, and measurements. Many solutions of interest also obey inequality constraints, including nonnegativity, monotonicity, and absence of arbitrage, which equality conditioning cannot enforce. We prove that conditioning a Gaussian process prior jointly on linear equality observations and a finite-dimensional inequality event is equivalent to conditioning sequentially in terms of Borel measures on the solution space. The physics-informed posterior is therefore a valid prior for the inequality update at virtual points. The combined law is non-Gaussian yet computable through truncated-Gaussian moments, and neither the PDE conditioning nor the inequality update requires modification. We evaluated the construction on a Poisson benchmark, option-price surfaces, and air-quality fields. Under incomplete boundary data, a monotonicity constraint lowered the error of a two-dimensional Poisson reconstruction by $63\%$. On a real S&P 500 option chain thinned to $20$ retained quotes, no-arbitrage constraints reduced held-out extrapolation error by $22\%$ and cut the calendar-arbitrage rate from $10\%$ to $1\%$. On four real air-quality snapshots, nonnegativity reduced a Gaussian moment-based sub-zero-tail proxy by $74\%$ at the sparsest monitor count. Changes in mean accuracy and constraint diagnostics differed across data regimes. The probability of the noisy virtual constraint event under the equality posterior measures agreement with the specified bounds before the update. The construction turns admissibility from a post-processing step into conditioning information for probabilistic PDE solvers.

papers.title: Improved screening of doped ZrO$_2$ catalysts for CO$_2$ hydrogenation from graph-based machine learning
papers.abstract: Dopants can tune the activity of zirconia-based CO$_2$ hydrogenation catalysts through changes in adsorbate and transition-state (TS) energetics. Computing these quantities with density functional theory (DFT) becomes expensive when several dopants, reaction intermediates, and TSs must be screened. Here, we further develop the graph-based machine learning method Wasserstein Weisfeiler-Lehman Gaussian Process Regression (WWL-GPR): we introduce additional electronic-structure and local-environment features relevant for oxide surfaces and use the resulting model to predict adsorption and TS energies on ZrO$_2$(101) surfaces doped with Al$^{3+}$, Cd$^{2+}$, Ga$^{3+}$, In$^{3+}$, and Zn$^{2+}$. Adsorbate-surface structures are represented as attributed graphs that combine bonds connectivity and features. We benchmark WWL-GPR against thermodynamic scaling relations (TSR) for reaction intermediates and Bronsted-Evans-Polanyi relations (BEP) for TSs, and then propagate the predicted energies to microkinetic CH$_3$OH-yield estimates. WWL-GPR consistently improves the prediction of reaction intermediate energetics relative to linear scaling approaches and provides TS estimates that are competitive with BEP-based models. These improvements become especially relevant when the predicted energetics are propagated through the reaction network. Microkinetic calculations show that WWL-GPR-derived energies give CH$_3$OH yields closer to DFT-derived yields than the linear-relation workflow. Degree-of-rate-control analysis links the activity errors to dopant-dependent rate-controlling steps, including HCOO* formation, H$_2$COOH* dissociation, and H$_3$CO* formation. These results support WWL-GPR as a data-efficient surrogate for connecting atomistic energetics with catalyst-screening observables on doped oxide surfaces.

papers.title: SimVTA: Simulation-Grounded Video-Trajectory Alignment for Driving World Action Models
papers.abstract: Driving world action models (WAMs) learn from paired trajectories and future observations. Post-training with reinforcement learning allows the policy to explore alternative trajectories and improve planning using driving rewards. However, driving logs contain future videos only for the recorded trajectories, leaving these alternatives without corresponding visual supervision. Thus, we introduce SimVTA, a simulation-grounded post-training framework that combines trajectory optimization with video supervision. First, we sample candidate trajectories for each observation and use a real-world simulator (e.g., World Engine) to render future videos for high-reward candidates in real-world scenes reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). Under a limited rendering budget, we prioritize video supervision for higher-error futures among these rendered candidates. Finally, we optimize trajectory planning with Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) and use a flow-matching loss on the matched videos to update shared representations. At inference time, the model predicts trajectories directly, without simulator calls. On NAVSIM v1, applying SimVTA to a WAM initialization improves PDMS from 86.2 to 91.3 (+5.1). It achieves 88.2 EPDMS on NAVSIM v2 and an average HD-Score of 38.8 in closed-loop evaluation on HUGSIM. Ablations show that updating shared representations with video supervision improves planning, while prioritizing higher-error futures among high-reward trajectories further improves performance.

Local patch memory supplies view-specific appearance, while recurrent global memory provides scene context. Footprint-guided retrieval selects historical patches under a fixed local read budget. Under matched retrieval and read budgets, GLIMPSE improves geometric correspondence and photometric consistency over deterministic positional transport.

papers.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
papers.abstract: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schrödinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

Doubly stochastic optimization with reduced ancestor sets achieves polylogarithmic complexity per iteration.

papers.title: Thyroid Nodule Segmentation in Ultrasound Images with Conformal Uncertainty Estimation
papers.abstract: Thyroid nodules affect a large proportion of the general population. Although most are benign, a non-negligible fraction is malignant. We address thyroid ultrasound nodule segmentation as the first stage of a pipeline that also includes malignancy classification and metastatic risk prediction. We adopt DeepLabV3+, whose Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP) captures multi-scale context, with an EfficientNet-B5 backbone for its accuracy-efficiency trade-off. Additionally, we test three channel-attention modules: Squeeze-and-Excitation, CBAM and Grouped Channel Attention (GCA), paired with two loss formulations (Dice-BCE and Boundary).\\ Since binary masks do not indicate prediction confidence, we wrap the trained model with a split conformal prediction layer that produces pixel-level uncertainty maps with statistical coverage guarantees.\\ We evaluate all configurations on the TN3K public benchmark using a fixed split and directly compare them with state-of-the-art methods. The plain backbone already improves upon previously reported results, with CBAM + Dice-BCE emerging as the best overall configuration.

The conformal procedures considered produce valid prediction intervals at every node of the hierarchy and the algorithm CP-MNR-Nested successfully accounts for the time-varying hierarchical structure of the data.

papers.title: Beyond Successful Robot Demonstrations: Learning from Human Interactions and Modeling Failure Dynamics
papers.abstract: Action-conditioned world models offer a promising foundation for generalist robotic intelligence by predicting the consequences of actions. However, existing robotic datasets provide limited coverage of the diverse interaction dynamics required for generalizable world modeling. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer complementary interaction experience, yet the embodiment gap between human hands and robotic manipulators hinders effective cross-embodiment learning. Meanwhile, the predominance of successful demonstrations leaves failure dynamics substantially underrepresented, limiting the ability of world models to anticipate unsuccessful executions. To address these limitations, we introduce HF-WM, an action-conditioned world model that combines Human interaction learning with Failure-aware post-training. To bridge the embodiment gap, we develop a dual-branch framework that couples video generation with auxiliary pointflow prediction, using stabilized pointflow as a unified motion representation across human and robot interactions while suppressing egocentric camera motion. To improve failure modeling, we further perform Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) post-training on perturbed actions derived from successful demonstrations, guided by action alignment and physical plausibility rewards, enabling the model to learn plausible failure dynamics without paired ground-truth videos. Extensive experiments demonstrate that HF-WM achieves state-of-the-art performance in action-conditioned video generation and exhibits strong utility for policy evaluation in downstream robotic tasks.

Raman spectra provided complimentary support for a systematic increase of the hematite phase on increasing the Eu/Ba ratio. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy informed the presence of oxygen deficiency and surface defects, and charge state of Ba and Fe/Eu ions close to +2 and +3, respectively. The material showed direct optical transitions with band gap in the range of 2.25-3.09 eV. The increase of Eu/Ba ratio systematically increased the saturation magnetization from 84.44 emu g-1 to 57.68 emu g-1 at 3 K and 67.09 emu g-1 to 43.42 emu g-1 at 300 K, along with remarkable enhancement of the coercivity (914- 3656 Oe at 3 K and 1996-4862 Oe at 300 K). Electrical conductivity increased from 10-11-10-10 Sm-1 at 30 K to 10-5 -10-4 Sm-1 at 300 K. The electrical conductivity analysis reveals the Efros-Shklovsky-type variable-range hopping mechanism at the low-temperature region, whereas the Mott variable range hopping mechanism is applicable near to room temperature. The analysis of current-voltage characteristics provided electrode to sample interfacial barrier height of 0.27-0.74 eV. The material exhibited novel magneto-electronic properties (bi-stable electronic switching and its transformation in the temperature scale, magnetoresistance and magnetoelectric coupling) which are highly useful for spintronic devices. papers.title: A Scalable Learned Iterative Solver for Nonlinear MPC via Temporal Decomposition
papers.abstract: Nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) can be applied to large nonlinear systems with complex objectives while enforcing constraints, but the cost of solving the underlying optimization problems limits real-time application for systems with fast dynamics or many states. Neural networks can reduce this online cost by approximating the control law, but may violate constraints and typically require many precomputed optimizer solutions for training. The learning-based iterative solver for constrained optimization (LISCO) instead learns to predict primal-dual steps toward satisfaction of the Karush-Kuhn-Tucker (KKT) conditions through self-supervised training without precomputed solutions, but its dense, monolithic architecture grows with the prediction horizon. We remove this horizon dependence by exploiting the temporal structure of the problem in the solver architecture, which makes the network size independent of the horizon while leaving the training loss and the solver iteration unchanged. A closed-loop resampling strategy further aligns the training distribution with closed-loop operation at no additional sampling cost. On an economic NMPC benchmark of a CSTR cascade, the proposed solver scales to larger problems than monolithic LISCO and achieves median speedups of up to a factor of four over IPOPT. In closed loop, it achieves comparable control performance to IPOPT with no observed constraint violations.

papers.title: Collective Autonomous Vehicle Routing Needs Social Awareness for Coexistence with Human Drivers
papers.abstract: Collective Autonomous Vehicle (AV) route choices in real-world traffic networks can create externalities for Human-Driven Vehicles (HDVs), as routes that benefit AVs may increase travel times for other road users. To address this, we introduce a social component, the marginal cost, to the selfish travel time AV reward. Marginal cost captures an AV's impact on other road users by comparing their travel times with those in a counterfactual simulation in which the AV is removed.   We study AV route choice in mixed-autonomy traffic settings using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL), where AVs learn routing policies through repeated interactions with the traffic environment. Experiments on the real-world networks of Ingolstadt and Provins show that incorporating marginal cost into the AV reward not only limits the increase in HDV travel times and shortens AV travel times relative to selfish AV routing, but also improves overall system performance. In Ingolstadt, selfish routing of 40\% AVs increases the travel times of other vehicles by 1.7\%, and this drops to 1.1\% when the social reward is included. Interestingly, not only does overall system performance improve, but the AVs are also better off when acting socially.This effect is consistent across tested cities, penetration rates, and replications, yet when the weight of the social component in the reward increases, the system fails to reach the desired performance.   For a more scalable approach to social AV routing in mixed-autonomy traffic, we compute the marginal cost only for the AVs whose route choices most affect the traffic system. This reduces the number of counterfactual simulations and achieves similar performance at a significantly lower computational cost. Our results suggest that AV routing should go beyond selfish rewards and, for the benefit of all traffic participants, include a social component in its objective.

papers.title: ManeuverFlow: Maneuver Hypothesis Generation with Future Evidence for Trajectory Evaluation and Refinement in End-to-End Autonomous Driving
papers.abstract: End-to-end planning in complex scenes must model diverse driving intentions and select the most appropriate trajectory using scene context and future risks. However, multi-query regression may collapse to one mode, while anchor-based and generative planners share a scaling bottleneck: small candidate sets limit maneuver coverage or discovery of high-quality trajectories, whereas large sets increase generation and scoring costs. We propose ManeuverFlow to generate trajectories for distinct intentions in one step and evaluate and refine them using current and future evidence. The model selects relevant maneuver modes, draws corresponding noise from the Gaussian mixture prior, and maps it to intention-specific trajectories through a maneuver-routed mixture-of-experts MeanFlow field. Current features and future features predicted by the world model are aggregated along each candidate path into trajectory-specific evidence for PDM-factor prediction. Using the same evidence, the refiner predicts local Frenet residuals for selected candidates; refined and retained candidates are then jointly re-scored for selection. With a lightweight TransFuser-style ResNet-34 backbone, ManeuverFlow achieves 90.6 PDMS and 90.1 EPDMS on NAVSIM v1/v2 navtest, respectively. On WorldEngine's recent 3DGS closed-loop benchmark, it attains the highest listed PDMS$^\ast$ scores of 75.19 and 74.58 under logged and IDM-controlled traffic, respectively. papers.abstract: Thyroid nodule malignancy assessment relies on ultrasound imaging, yet current risk stratification systems suffer from substantial interobserver variability, contributing to a high rate of unnecessary biopsies. To complement point predictions with uncertainty estimates, Cross-Conformal Prediction with label-conditional guarantees is applied, flagging ambiguous cases for clinical review rather than forcing a binary decision. Experiments are conducted on TN5000, a publicly available ultrasound dataset of thyroid nodules. After Spearman correlation filtering, 36 features are retained and the GAM achieves an AUC of $0.89$, a sensitivity of $0.83$, and a specificity of $0.82$ on the validation set. At a significance level $ε=0.09$, selected to ensure empirical coverage guarantees on both classes, 63\% of nodules on the test set receive a certain (i.e., single-label) prediction, with conditional precision of $0.94$ for certain malignant and conditional Negative Predictive Value (NPV) of $0.73$ for certain benign cases, while the remaining 37\% are referred to the clinician.

papers.title: SBNO : Schrödinger Bridge Neural Operator for the Forward and Inverse Problems under Missing Information
papers.abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE) surrogate modeling often relies on either dense observations or access to governing equations/physics constraints. In practice, observations can be sparse and partial, and the underlying physics may be partially specified or unavailable. We introduce SBNO, an equation-free paired-data diffusion bridge matching framework that learns conditional operators for both forward and inverse PDE problems under partial observations. SBNO uses diffusion Schrödinger bridge matching to learn a pair of time-dependent drifts from a mask-aware endpoint coupling that preserves empirical input-solution pairing during training and supports both PDE-task directions within a single framework. At inference time, SBNO produces a deterministic point reconstruction by integrating the probability-flow ODE constructed from the learned drift pair, without inference-time observation or PDE guidance-weight tuning. On five PDE benchmarks with 5% observations, SBNO achieves superior or comparable accuracy to baselines while demonstrating lower test-instance error dispersion. Furthermore, SBNO is at least $9.7 \times$ faster and reduces GPU memory by at least $4.3 \times$ compared to guided-diffusion baselines.

papers.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
papers.abstract: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation. However, this Generate-Execute-Feedback paradigm relies on reactive trial-and-error, where costly and time-consuming executions introduce severe feedback delays, throttling evolutionary progress under explosively expanding search space. To address this challenge, we propose JANUS, a framework that unifies future outcomes forecasting and past experience reflection through a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop driven by a co-evolving world model. Within an evolving graph, the research agent proposes candidates while world model scores them by forecasting value improvement, information gain, and exploration utility, then accordingly selects, refines, or prunes branches prior to execution. After receiving ground-truth feedback, JANUS distills experience into evolving skills: hierarchical skills for research agent, exploration-strategy skills for world model, and their coordination protocols. This mechanism enables continual co-evolution: the research agent sharpens candidate generation while the world model refines its predictive judgment over extended horizons. Extensive evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite and real research tasks demonstrate that JANUS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving both higher evolving efficiency and ceiling.

papers.title: Grounded-Dreamer: Robot Learning from World Model Synthetic Data with Physical Grounding
papers.abstract: Scaling robot manipulation policies requires large amounts of diverse, action-labeled data, yet collecting such data in the real world remains expensive and difficult to scale. Existing methods either depend on human teleoperation, rely on simulation with limited visual realism, or use human videos that lack embodiment-specific annotations. In this paper, we introduce Grounded-Dreamer, a framework for synthesizing physically grounded robot manipulation data with video world models while avoiding human teleoperation demonstrations. Grounded-Dreamer combines the visual realism of generative video models with simulator physics engines. Starting from a small set of real images depicting robot task initial states, our method automatically reconstructs task-relevant objects and camera geometry, aligns them in simulation, and collects physically valid trajectories. These trajectories are used to post-train both a video world model and an inverse dynamics model, enabling the generation of visually realistic robot manipulation videos and corresponding robot actions from real images. To filter physically implausible rollouts, Grounded-Dreamer replays generated trajectories in the reconstructed simulation and retains only those that successfully complete the tasks. The real-world robot policies are trained solely on the grounded synthetic trajectories without any human demonstrations. Empirical results in real-world tasks demonstrate that Grounded-Dreamer can synthesize physically grounded data and substantially facilitate policy learning without requiring human teleoperation effort.

papers.title: Low-Rank Kolmogorov-Arnold Generator Flows for Interpretable Operator Learning
papers.abstract: Neural operators that learn physical laws from data should generalize beyond their training distribution and expose the learned law in closed form. The Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator achieves both for position-dependent dynamics by learning a dense pseudo-differential symbol over all positions and frequencies, at a cost that grows with the square of the resolution and with closed forms that must be read out by hand. This dense symbol is unnecessary: a finite-order variable-coefficient differential operator has a symbol whose separation rank is bounded by the number of its coefficient functions, independently of the resolution, and the symbols that this network learns on its own benchmarks have rank two. We introduce the Kolmogorov-Arnold flow (KAFlow), which learns the generator of a physical operator as a low-rank symbol built from univariate Kolmogorov-Arnold functions, fixes the gauge of these functions so that every term has a unique place, integrates the dynamics with exact exponential integrators, and distills its closed form automatically. On the synthetic benchmarks of the Kolmogorov-Arnold neural operator, KAFlow lowers the out-of-distribution loss by 3.4 to 11 times and recovers every coefficient to within 10^-4 without symbolic templates, reaching the precision floor of the data. On long-horizon quantum dynamics, it lowers the state infidelity by up to 6 orders of magnitude, and by 30 times when trained only on position and momentum measurements. KAFlow also learns a variable-order fractional operator 15 times more accurately than existing operator networks and discovers nonlocal, fractional and non-polynomial dispersion relations on which sparse regression fails.

papers.title: Evidential Multimodal Transformers with Dempster-Shafer Fusion for Emotion Recognition
papers.abstract: Softmax-based multimodal emotion recognition methods often assign high confidence even when sensor data are corrupted or contradictory, for example when facial expressions suggest positive valence while vocal prosody indicates negative arousal. We present an Evidential Multimodal Transformer with Dempster-Shafer Fusion (EMT-DS) that addresses this problem through formal uncertainty quantification. EMT-DS models predictions as Subjective Opinions (Dirichlet distributions), separating epistemic uncertainty (lack of evidence) from aleatoric uncertainty (sensor noise). Modality-specific transformer encoders produce belief mass distributions that are fused with Dempster's Rule of Combination, which normalizes the joint belief mass by a conflict coefficient 1/(1-c), so that contradictory evidence is explicitly quantified as conflict and the fused prediction becomes diffuse rather than being forced into an unjustified consensus. Under subject-independent and speaker-independent evaluation on four benchmarks, EMT-DS achieves 84.3% accuracy on IEMOCAP versus 81.7% for the best baseline (p < 0.01), 82.4% on DEAP under leave-one-subject-out evaluation versus 78.1%, and 96.8% on the highly imbalanced KEMDy20, and it improves accuracy on CMU-MOSEI by 2.4 points over the strongest evidential baseline. In controlled ablation, it reduces Expected Calibration Error from 0.153 (softmax transformer) to 0.042. It maintains 71.2% accuracy under severe Gaussian noise on audio features (sigma = 1.0), where attention baselines drop to 45.3%, and degrades gracefully when entire modalities are absent. The fusion step has O(MK^2) complexity, compared with O(M^2 d^2) for cross-modal attention. The learned conflict metric also flags likely errors: reviewing 20% of samples captures 80% of misclassifications, which supports selective prediction in clinical and safety-critical systems.

papers.title: Spatial Prediction with Guided Diffusion
papers.abstract: Spatial prediction is a critically important task in data analyses that involve spatially or spatio-temporally-referenced data. It is commonly carried out using hierarchical models, which comprise a process model describing the latent process of interest, and a data model describing how the process is observed. The target quantity is the predictive distribution, which is the conditional distribution of the latent spatial process given the observed data. Unfortunately, the predictive distribution is rarely available in closed form and can be difficult to sample from. Here, we show how recent developments in guided diffusion modelling from machine learning can address a wide class of problems in spatial prediction when the likelihood function derived from the data model is known and differentiable, possibly after relaxation. To show the versatility of the approach, we apply it to both Gaussian and non-Gaussian process models and a variety of data models that describe direct partial observations, linear and areal aggregates, counts, right censoring, and area-exceedance functionals. Where possible, we validate the framework against exact and Markov-chain-Monte-Carlo (MCMC)-derived predictive distributions. We demonstrate our approach on several simulation studies and in a controlled experiment of methane-flux inversion over the UK and Ireland. We show that guided diffusion can sample from the correct predictive distribution in a variety of settings, that it can be applied to models where MCMC is intractable, and that it scales well with the dimensionality of the latent process.

papers.title: Sequential Conformal Calibration under Recursive Selection
papers.abstract: Conformal prediction provides finite-sample, distribution-free coverage guarantees that can support decision-making in specific settings. In multistage problems, earlier decisions determine the populations relevant to later calibration. When later scores are refit using earlier calibration results, reusing those cases for ranking need not preserve exchangeability with a surviving test case. We study sequential conformal calibration with a fresh fold at each stage: conditional on earlier folds, the selected fold scores and the surviving test score are exchangeable. This yields finite-sample coverage guarantees for every prefix of the decision sequence. For atomless survivor score distributions, we derive a universal Binomial-thinned Beta chain for the realized coverage process. Its law depends only on fold sizes and target levels, even under predictable refitting, and yields exact coverage slack, abstention probabilities, and calibration-conditional guarantees. We further characterize the tradeoff between freshness and data reuse. For fixed scores, strict-survivor reuse is exactly valid. For adaptive scores refit using past calibration data, reusing survivors can incur worst-case rank loss, while blocked designs provide an intermediate option between full reuse and stagewise fresh folds. As a case study, we apply the framework to serial multi-echelon inventory problem and propose a sequential conditional-quantile formulation. Each stock level is learned as a context-dependent quantile of cumulative demand among scenarios satisfying earlier no-backlog constraints. We connect these targets to common-shift stationarity and derive decision-level implications for the resulting calibrated policies. In a three-echelon simulation, fresh-fold refitting achieves 81.98% final-prefix coverage against an 81.82% target while reducing mean cost by 5.5% relative to the Bonferroni baseline.

papers.abstract: Visual world models predict the consequences of actions from images, but planning with them is typically done by optimizers such as CEM and MPPI. This paper revisits kinodynamic sampling-based motion planning for world models, using the learned model as the propagator of a tree search in latent space. Our key insight is that the sampling strategies devised for high-dimensional search in configuration space apply directly to the latent space of a world model, where they rapidly expand through intermediate states that myopic optimizers never sample. We present two exploration strategies for the high-dimensional latent space, nearest-neighbor-guided RRT and projection-based KPIECE, with GPU-native batched expansion for efficient device utilization. We evaluate with an off-the-shelf DINO-WM on four simulated domains and a real-world block-pushing task. Our approaches match or exceed the success rate of CEM and MPPI at up to 13.8x lower planning time in simulation, and improve the success rate by 20% on the real robot.

papers.title: Robust Langevin Sampling under State-Dependent Heavy-Tailed Noise with Applications to LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Existing convergence guarantees for non-log-concave sampling with stochastic gradient Langevin Monte Carlo (SG-LMC) typically assume globally Lipschitz gradients and uniformly bounded noise variance. Both assumptions can fail even in elementary sampling problems, and relaxing them better reflects practical applications such as Bayesian fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs). We relax both assumptions through generalized smoothness and our proposed state-dependent heavy-tailed oracle with finite $p$-th moments, $1<p\leq 2$. The oracle permits infinite variance when $p<2$ and includes the Blum-Gladyshev (BG-0) condition. We study these relaxations separately and jointly, proposing three methods. Under globally Lipschitz gradients, robust LMC (R-LMC) handles the proposed oracle through geometric-median centering and residual clipping. With exact gradients, adaptive LMC (A-LMC) controls discretization error under generalized smoothness. Robust adaptive LMC (RA-LMC) addresses both relaxations through robust estimation and a noise-aware step size. For all three methods, we establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees in Fisher information (FI) without assuming dissipativity or a functional inequality. Synthetic experiments demonstrate FI convergence and the benefit of each mechanism. Bayesian fine-tuning experiments with LLMs and vision-language models support our oracle model and show that RA-LMC matches or outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in accuracy and uncertainty quantification.

papers.title: Adaptive Node Distribution via Probability Density Functions for Birkhoff Pseudospectral Trajectory Optimisation
papers.abstract: Pseudospectral methods are a powerful framework for spacecraft trajectory optimisation that rely on fixed, problem-independent collocation nodes such as Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto (LGL) nodes. These nodes are located according to polynomial root distributions, which can result in insufficient resolution in regions of high dynamical activity, such as those encountered during collision avoidance manoeuvres. This paper presents an adaptive node distribution strategy for Birkhoff pseudospectral trajectory optimisation, where the collocation nodes are placed according to a probability density function derived from the thrust magnitude profile of the spacecraft. By concentrating nodes in regions of high dynamical variation, the proposed method simultaneously achieves feasibility preservation and improved convergence with fewer nodes in a collision avoidance case study when compared to the universal Birkhoff method, with Model Predictive Control serving as an independent validation comparator. The case study highlights the practical consequences of inter-node constraint violations and validates the adaptive node scheme as a robust and efficient alternative for fuel-optimal spacecraft manoeuvre design.

papers.title: Physics-Informed Neural Network for Predicting pH-Sensitive Drug Release Kinetics and Selective Cytotoxicity of Docetaxel Nanocarriers
papers.abstract: Background: Docetaxel (DTX) is a potent chemotherapeutic agent whose clinical utility is limited by poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, and significant off-target toxicity. Nanoparticle-based delivery systems offer a promising solution, yet the complex, multi-parametric relationships governing pH-sensitive drug release and selective cytotoxicity remain incompletely understood. Methods: A Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) framework was developed integrating experimental data from 90 DTX nanocarrier formulations spanning eight platform categories with governing ordinary differential equations (ODEs) for pH-dependent drug release kinetics. The dual-output architecture simultaneously predicted cumulative release profiles at physiological (pH 7.4) and tumor-mimetic (pH 5.5-6.5) conditions alongside selectivity indices. Results: The PINN achieved R 2 = 0.94 ± 0.03 for release prediction and R 2 = 0.89 ± 0.04 for selectivity prediction, representing an approximately 23% reduction (evaluated on a held-out test set of ~14 formulations; larger independent datasets are needed to confirm this magnitude) in prediction error relative to conventional neural networks. Feature importance analysis identified pH sensitivity as the dominant predictor (40.5% relative importance), followed by zeta potential (28.3%) and nanoparticle size (18.7%). The HA-Ag-PB@DTX hybrid nanocarrier emerged as the optimal formulation, demonstrating a selectivity index of 18.2 and pH release ratio of 3.85. Conclusion: This work establishes a robust computational framework for accelerating rational design of smart nanomedicines with predictable release kinetics and therapeutic selectivity, providing hypothesis-generating guidance for tumor microenvironment-responsive DTX delivery, pending wet-lab and in vivo validation of the top-ranked formulations.
